cta.lede: On a call, with a senior strategist. We scope your first website maintenance client and agree how we work behind you.

stages.breaks: Taking on a site without an audit.
stages.why: Old plugins, no backups and unknown logins surface on the first bad day, after you promised care.
stages.does: We audit every site first, list what is outdated and unprotected, and agree a baseline with you before care starts.

stages.why: One bad plugin update takes a client offline and the call comes to you.
stages.does: Updates run on a copy first. Anything that breaks is held back and reported to you before it touches the live site.

stages.breaks: Having backups that nobody has tried to restore.
stages.why: A backup you have never restored is a hope, not a plan.
stages.does: Off-site copies, a restore test on a schedule, and a record of the result you can show your client.

stages.breaks: Letting small requests sit in an inbox.
stages.why: Edits that are forgotten or done for free eat the margin on the plan.
stages.does: Requests go in one queue, are logged against the plan and are quoted when they fall outside it.

stages.breaks: Sending a task list instead of a report.
stages.why: A list of updates proves effort, not value, and clients cancel plans that look like nothing.
stages.does: A short report with Done, Watch and Next, plus the one suggested change, in your branding.
